name: Nu Holdings
thesis: Latin America's leading digital bank (Brazil + Mexico + Colombia). Three engines: (1) customer acquisition, where Brazil is now a saturation/monetization story and the leading indicator has migrated to net adds and primary-banking share in Mexico and Colombia; (2) ARPAC ramping as customers layer credit and investment products onto the deposit relationship, with near-zero incremental cost-to-serve translating revenue growth into operating leverage; (3) exceptional ROE driven by expanding risk-adjusted NIM, seasonal NPL ratios kept in hand, and a prudent capital cushion preserved through the credit cycle. Bet: 25%+ revenue growth with ROE crossing 30%, where durable Brazil profitability — earned on risk-adjusted spread, not scale leverage — funds the Mexico/Colombia land-grab without forcing underwriting compromise.
key_driver: Customer count × ARPAC × NIM with NPL controlled
chart_priorities: Products per active customer by country (BR / MX / CO)
Credit exposure mix by product x country
Monthly ARPAC by country (BR / MX / CO)
NPL ratio by country and bucket (15-90d + 90d+ : BR / MX / CO)

tier_1_kpis.name: Product penetration by country (products per active customer: BR / MX / CO)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: MX or CO products-per-active flat QoQ for 2 consecutive Qs while BR also fails to expand
tier_1_kpis.source: earnings release / investor presentation segment slides

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit exposure mix by product x country (% of loan book: credit card / personal loan / secured x BR / MX / CO)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: MX or CO credit-card share of book grows >500bps QoQ without matching NPL coverage build
tier_1_kpis.source: earnings release / investor presentation segment slides

tier_1_kpis.name: Return on equity (ROE)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: ROE <25% for 2 consecutive Qs, or sustained downward trend over 3+ Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM net of cost of risk)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Risk-adjusted NIM compresses >100bps YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (precursor to ROE break)

tier_1_kpis.name: Monthly ARPAC by country (USD: BR / MX / CO)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: BR ARPAC growth <15% YoY or MX ARPAC growth <30% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: Total customers (millions)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Net adds <5M per quarter for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: NPL ratio by country and bucket (15-90d + 90d+ : BR / MX / CO)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Consolidated (15-90d + 90d+) NPL rises >150bps YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (YoY framing strips seasonality; absolute level secondary as the underwriting mix evolves), or MX/CO total NPL diverges >200bps above BR YoY-change while their books are still scaling

thesis_breakers_qualitative: ROE sustained below 25% (core profitability engine breaking)
Risk-adjusted NIM compression (precursor to ROE break — NIM pressure or rising cost of risk)
Product penetration in MX/CO stalls (cross-sell engine fails to replicate BR playbook)
Credit exposure tilts toward unsecured in MX/CO faster than NPL coverage can absorb
BR ARPAC growth <15% YoY (monetization story stalls in the saturated core)
Consolidated NPL (15-90d + 90d+) rises >150bps YoY sustained (credit-cycle break, isolated from underwriting-mix evolution via YoY framing)
Revenue YoY growth rate decelerates >80% QoQ (e.g. from +50% YoY to <+10% YoY) — sharp loss of top-line momentum, not outright contraction

break_rules.narrative: ROE falls below 25% for 2 consecutive quarters — the core profitability engine (expanding risk-adjusted NIM + operating leverage) is breaking down.

break_rules.kpi_name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM net of cost of risk)
break_rules.narrative: Risk-adjusted NIM compresses more than 100bps YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — precursor to ROE break, signals either NIM pressure or rising cost of risk eroding unit economics.
Revenue YoY growth rate decelerates by more than 80% from the prior quarter's YoY growth rate — sharp loss of growth momentum.

break_rules.kpi_name: NPL ratio by country and bucket (15-90d + 90d+ : BR / MX / CO)
break_rules.narrative: Consolidated NPL (15-90d early-stage + 90d+ late-stage, summed) rises more than 150bps YoY for 2 consecutive quarters. YoY framing is intentional — the underwriting mix is actively evolving (geographic and product expansion), so a static absolute threshold misreads either seasonality or a deliberately riskier book that is still being priced correctly. YoY change isolates credit-cycle deterioration from underwriting-mix drift.

business_model_rules.narrative: 90d+ NPL > 7% for 2Q — credit-quality break; their underwriting thesis depends on the 5-6% historical range holding.
Monthly ARPAC < $10 for 2Q — cross-sell stalling; expanding ARPAC is the unit-economics flywheel.
Activity rate < 82% for 2Q — customers becoming dormant; engagement-flywheel signal.
15-90d NPL > 5% for 2Q — leading indicator of cohort credit deterioration; fires 1-2Q before 90d+ trips.
